how_to_read: Base trial/ai-wave f71d8e0. The base field is the commit the file was last written on; today and expect are the base's (its Python readers, and protocol 4's rows through a binary that reads them as the base's did). The rules are WAVE_AL_CONTRACT.md.

paths: row = flight.record_to_row and row_to_record in protocol 5's layout; python = build_evidence(detectors='python'); rust_raw = server_detect.server_report; rust_raw_v4 = tensorquill-server detect given protocol 4's rows (experiments/protocol-v5/flight_v4.py), as an older SDK sends them; rust_sdk = build_evidence(detectors='rust'); live_server = a protocol 5 release server fed by flight.send_file, read from the rank's incidents.json and its stored objects; runs = python -m tensorquill runs; mcp_get_series = the MCP tool get_series; capture = tensorquill.init and Session.log; today = the base's readers.

Sections 1 and 2: row is what record_to_row must give at row.step (typed columns as [name, value] pairs in stored order, non-finite floats as the sink's strings, null for a null column or a null struct; probe_json as text; extra as extra_json parsed, null for none), and row_to_record(record_to_row(r)) == r with the map's order kept. expect is today's engines on clean_records (or on records when there are none): every engine path must report that on records. today is the base on records (never recomputed).
known_difference: a path whose expect is today's, not the clean records' report, and why (the owner's word).
Section 4: expect is written from the contract's rules; series maps a scalar name to [step, value] points in step order.
measured: the results file under experiments/protocol-v5/ that shows the case's today on a real server.

cases.name: layers_model_order
cases.about: activation_spike leads with the earliest block in forward order; the typed map keeps the model's order (model.layers.2 before model.layers.10), which sorting would not

cases.name: layers_empty_map
cases.about: a router-only capture writes layers {} on every record (granite-router-only.jsonl): an empty typed map, no extra_json

cases.name: layers_non_finite_strings
cases.about: the sink's strings for NaN and Inf in struct fields are held, as non-finite floats; non_finite names the layer in both engines

cases.name: layers_field_bool
cases.about: a bool in a field is refused: the field is null in the struct and travels in extra_json under layers.<name>.<field>; the layer is skipped by the activation kinds (std absent)

cases.name: layers_field_other_string
cases.about: a string other than the sink's three ("NaN") is refused like a bool

cases.name: layers_field_missing
cases.about: a missing field is a null struct field and reads back absent; no extra_json

cases.name: layers_field_extra
cases.about: a field the struct does not name travels in extra_json; its value is still read for non_finite (Python reads every value of a layer; detect.rs' visitor ORs every key today)

cases.name: layers_field_null
cases.about: an explicit null field is refused, so it reads back as null and not absent

cases.name: layers_entry_not_object
cases.about: an entry that is not an object keeps its place as a null struct and travels whole in extra_json; it is absent to every detector, in both engines

cases.name: layers_name_arrow_cannot_encode
cases.about: a name with a lone surrogate cannot be a key: the entry travels only in extra_json and is read after the column's entries

known_difference.rust_raw_v4: not fixed (the owner, Nov 24): on protocol 4's row the whole layers map is in layers_json, the name written as the JSON escape of a lone surrogate, which Rust's JSON reader refuses, so Rust reads no layer of that row, while Python reads the record's layers; pinned on each side by lane AL-S1

cases.name: layers_int_in_float_field
cases.about: an integer in a Float64 field is held as a float: the round trip holds by == (0 == 0.0), the JSON text does not ("0" against "0.0"), as for wave AJ's maps

cases.name: layers_value_not_object
